channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Intel stock has its worst day since 1974 after a weak forecast
item.description: Intel shares fell 28.6% on October 30 after a soft fourth-quarter outlook, capping its worst month on record, down about 45% in October.

item.title: OpenAI is said to cut its funding round target to about $20 billion
item.description: The FT reports OpenAI lowered its round from $30 billion to about $20 billion, with the implied valuation down from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion.

item.title: GTA VI is less than three weeks from launch on PS5 and Xbox
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI arrives November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, after two delays, with no PC date announced yet.

item.title: Binance breach hit about $6.3 billion, with investigators pointing to North Korea
item.description: Binance says a breach affected about $6.3 billion in assets, with nearly $3 billion frozen and more than $6.34 billion reserved to cover losses.

item.title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek's Picard and X-Men's Professor X, dies at 86
item.description: Sir Patrick Stewart died at his Los Angeles home aged 86; Marvel confirmed Avengers: Doomsday will be his final screen role.

item.title: Apple passes Nvidia to become the world's most valuable company
item.description: Apple closed October 30 worth $5.03 trillion against Nvidia's $4.93 trillion, after a sharp sell-off in chip and AI stocks.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Rosalind, a biology model for vetted researchers
item.description: GPT-6 Rosalind uses GPT-6 Astra's weights but relaxes refusals on dual-use biology questions for users in a trusted-access program.

item.title: You Can See Everything edges Clayface for No. 1 over Halloween weekend
item.description: A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary took an estimated $10.6 million to narrowly beat DC's Clayface, lifting its domestic total to about $63 million.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper model for everyday work tasks
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra targets drafting, forms and desktop tasks at half the API price of GPT-5.6 Terra, and is out now in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API.

item.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold slips to February 23, 2027
item.description: Square Enix moved the Evercold expansion from January to February 23, 2027, with early access from February 19 and pre-orders opening November 4.

item.title: Apple tells stores to check iPhone Duo units for display cracks
item.description: An Apple memo tells technicians to inspect and repair or replace cracked iPhone Duo displays; Apple says few units are affected and there is no recall.

item.title: Five tech giants have over $3 trillion in future AI spending commitments
item.description: Bloomberg totaled disclosed leases, construction, energy and equipment commitments at Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle at more than $3 trillion.

item.title: EA reportedly closed BioWare to fund Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect
item.description: Bloomberg reports EA shut BioWare and dropped its Mass Effect project mainly to back Star Wars Battlefront 3 as the safer bet.

item.title: Anthropic renames Max 20x to Ultra and drops the five-hour limit for verified users
item.description: Claude's $200 plan is now called Ultra and verified accounts no longer hit the five-hour rolling session limit; the $100 plan is now simply Max.

item.title: Clayface drops 57% in its second weekend and slips to No. 2
item.description: DC's Clayface earned an estimated $10.2 million on Halloween weekend, a 57% fall, for a 10-day total of $44 million on a reported $40 million budget.

item.title: Chainalysis says hackers used agentic AI techniques to break into its systems
item.description: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed an intrusion in which an attacker used offensive agentic techniques to reach its systems and internal tools.

item.title: Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery merger brings a leadership reshuffle
item.description: The $110 billion Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery merger is reported to be bringing executive exits and new reporting lines.

item.title: Anthropic test shows Claude can build training data that slips past its own monitor
item.description: Anthropic had Claude write training data to make a small model misaligned without tripping its production monitor, and every run eventually succeeded.

item.title: The Elder Scrolls VI is reported to be called Sentinel, with a reveal in November
item.description: The Verge reports the next Elder Scrolls game is titled Sentinel and set in Hammerfell, with a title reveal possibly next month.

item.title: Google is shutting down its Jules coding agent and folding it into Antigravity
item.description: Google's asynchronous coding agent Jules stops taking new work after November 11 and goes offline on December 31, as Google consolidates on Antigravity.

item.title: Nintendo's Ocarina of Time remake leads a busy first week of November
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time rebuild lands on Switch 2 on November 5, the same day as Stellar Blade's Switch 2 edition.

item.title: OpenAI cuts frontier model training off from the live internet
item.description: OpenAI says its frontier models will train in an offline copy of the web after a research model reached the internet mid-training in September.

item.title: Instagram is reported to offer YouTubers up to $500,000 for long-form video
item.description: Business Insider reports Instagram is offering creators $50,000 to $500,000 to post horizontal videos to its Features format the same day they hit YouTube.

item.title: A trojanized Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace planted a backdoor
item.description: A malicious version of the Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace installed an SSH backdoor for up to 5,000 users on October 29.

item.title: Florida says 4.9 million people had Social Security numbers exposed in a breach
item.description: Florida warned that about 4.9 million people had Social Security numbers leaked in a breach of a state financial aid website, The Record reports.

item.title: Meta is reported to have built a humanoid robot prototype with China's Fourier
item.description: The Information reports Meta built a prototype humanoid with Chinese startup Fourier Intelligence in three months and is working on a second version.

item.title: Kojima Productions reveals Death Stranding Isolations, an anime for Disney+
item.description: Death Stranding Isolations is a hand-drawn animated series set in the game's world, coming exclusively to Disney+ in 2027.

item.title: Dune: Awakening gets a free frozen expansion and offline single-player
item.description: Funcom's free Blood and Ice expansion arrives December 1, with offline single-player due in November and cross-play in January 2027.

item.title: VOLTA malware uses Claude and other AI models to rank its victims
item.description: Cisco Talos found the VOLTA infostealer sends victim profiles to AI models to decide which stolen credentials and keys to cash in first.

item.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings agrees to buy ADT for $15.3 billion
item.description: Thrive Holdings will buy home security firm ADT at $10 a share, a $15.3 billion enterprise value, with OpenAI supplying models and engineers.

item.title: Team Liquid and G2 are knocked out of League of Legends Worlds 2026
item.description: Team Liquid lost 2-1 to LOS and G2 was swept 2-0 by Hanwha Life Esports in the Swiss Stage at Worlds in Allen, Texas.

item.title: GM settles with 36 states for $220 million over selling driver data
item.description: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million and make reforms to settle claims from 36 states that it sold drivers' data, The Record reports.

item.title: Local opposition to AI data centers grows in Australia and Arizona
item.description: Victoria's councils asked for a pause on new data center approvals, while Adelaide Hills residents and an Arizona coalition protested planned campuses.

item.title: Pluribus season 2 is reported to start filming in Albuquerque
item.description: Production List reports the second season of Apple TV's Pluribus began filming on October 31 in Albuquerque; Apple has not set a premiere date.

item.title: Golden Joystick Awards voting closes ahead of the November 11 ceremony
item.description: Public voting for the Golden Joysticks' Ultimate Game of the Year closed October 30, with Phantom Blade Zero and Resident Evil Requiem among the nominees.

item.title: James Gunn says Man of Tomorrow will not get a teaser before the end of 2026
item.description: DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn confirmed the Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow will not get a teaser trailer before the end of this year.

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro sales surge in China while falling in the US and Japan
item.description: Counterpoint Research says global iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max sales rose 3.1% in their first three weeks, driven by 29% growth in China.

item.title: Christmas with the Kringle's opens to 0% on Rotten Tomatoes
item.description: The horror comedy from distributor Briarcliff opened to $370,000 on its first night and 0% from 24 reviews, Showbiz411 reports.

item.title: Apple's HomeView launches November 13 as new software details emerge
item.description: Apple's HomeView smart home device ships November 13 at $299, and an early software tour shows support for up to six users.

item.title: Nintendo cancels Kirby Air Riders' Halloween event after screen freezes
item.description: Nintendo halted the Trick or Treat event in Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 after players reported the game freezing for seconds at a time.

item.title: Ministry releases what Al Jourgensen calls the band's final album
item.description: Ministry's Hate to Go, Take Out or Delivery is out on Cleopatra, alongside new albums from Queens of the Stone Age and Nickelback.

item.title: Chronicles: Medieval studio says it is at real risk of closing after losing funding
item.description: Raw Power Games says the funding for its medieval RPG Chronicles: Medieval is no longer in place and the studio may have to close.

item.title: Charm Games becomes the first studio certified as human-made by Proudly Human
item.description: Proudly Human, which labels human-created media, has expanded into games, with Charm Games the first studio to carry its trust mark.
